# [TASK] ai-service: token/span breakdown on the query-parsing response

## Task
Extend the query-parsing endpoint's response with a token/span breakdown so
the frontend can highlight without doing its own NLP.

## Scope
Response shape only — reuses #198's existing parsing endpoint/logic, adds a
field to its response.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] Response includes a list of `{ text, category, start, end }` spans covering connectors, negations, and entities (`AiServiceIntegrationTest.parseQueryExtractsFullFilterForMultiConstraintQuery`, `AiServiceIntegrationTest.parseQueryExtractsNegationAsADistinctFieldAndSpan`)
- [x] Span offsets are exact against the original submitted text, including non-ASCII input (`AiServiceIntegrationTest.parseQueryProducesExactSpanOffsetsForAnAccentedName`, `QuerySpanExtractorTest.extract_AccentedName_ProducesExactOffsets`)
- [x] A plain-title query returns an empty span list, not an error (`AiServiceIntegrationTest.parseQueryReturnsPlainTitleFallbackForATitleOnlyQuery`, `QuerySpanExtractorTest.extract_PlainTitleQuery_ReturnsEmptyList`)
- [x] Unit tests assert exact span boundaries for a multi-category query (`QuerySpanExtractorTest.extract_MultiCategoryQuery_ReturnsSpansInTextOrder`)

## Estimate
**Hours:** 4

## Notes
`QueryParsingService.parseWithSpans` calls the existing `#202` extraction,
then `QuerySpanExtractor` computes spans deterministically: plain string
search over the already-extracted filter, not asked of the model, because
offsets must be exact and a generative model cannot reliably report
character positions. `POST /api/v1/ai/search/query` returns
`QueryParseResponseDto{filter, spans}`. Offsets are UTF-16 code-unit
offsets, not byte offsets, matching JS string indexing so the frontend can
slice its own field value directly.
